default.cause: The trained class may be associated with a fungal, bacterial, viral, pest, or environmental problem. Confirm the cause locally.
default.symptoms: Compare spots, discoloration, wilting, mildew, lesions, and leaf distortion with a trusted crop-disease reference.
default.action: Separate affected plants, avoid spreading plant material, improve airflow, and consult an agronomist before treatment.
default.food_safety: Do not eat visibly diseased plant parts. CropAI cannot determine whether produce is safe to eat; follow local food-safety guidance.

healthy.cause: No disease pattern was found among the classes supported by this model.
healthy.symptoms: No supported disease signal was detected in the uploaded image.
healthy.action: Continue normal crop monitoring and rescan if visible changes develop.
healthy.food_safety: A healthy model result is not a food-safety certification. Wash produce and follow normal food-handling guidance.

early blight.cause: Commonly associated with the fungus Alternaria solani and conditions that leave foliage wet for long periods.
early blight.symptoms: Dark lesions, often with concentric rings, yellowing, and premature leaf loss.
early blight.action: Remove severely affected foliage, reduce leaf wetness, improve airflow, and confirm treatment locally.
early blight.food_safety: Do not eat affected leaves. Inspect harvested produce and follow local food-safety advice before consumption.

late blight.cause: Associated with the oomycete Phytophthora infestans and cool, wet conditions.
late blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding dark lesions, water-soaked areas, and possible white growth under humid conditions.
late blight.action: Isolate affected plants promptly, avoid handling wet foliage, and contact an agricultural specialist.
late blight.food_safety: Do not eat visibly affected produce. Discard questionable material according to local guidance.

powdery mildew.cause: A group of fungal pathogens favored by humid air and limited airflow.
powdery mildew.symptoms: White powder-like growth on leaf surfaces, curling, yellowing, or reduced vigor.
powdery mildew.action: Improve spacing and airflow, remove heavily affected leaves, and confirm an approved treatment.
powdery mildew.food_safety: Do not eat visibly diseased leaves. Wash edible produce and follow local food-safety guidance.

bacterial spot.cause: Bacterial pathogens can spread through splashing water, handling, and contaminated plant material.
bacterial spot.symptoms: Small dark or water-soaked spots that may merge and cause yellowing or fruit blemishes.
bacterial spot.action: Remove affected material, avoid overhead watering, sanitize tools, and seek local guidance.
bacterial spot.food_safety: Do not eat damaged or questionable parts. Food safety depends on the crop, severity, and local guidance.

mosaic virus.cause: Plant viruses are often spread by infected material or insect vectors.
mosaic virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark patterns, leaf distortion, stunting, and uneven growth.
mosaic virus.action: Remove infected plants where advised, control vectors, and avoid saving propagation material.
mosaic virus.food_safety: Do not eat visibly damaged plant parts. Ask local agricultural and food-safety authorities about the crop.
